what_it_changes: How much empty edge surrounds everything. This one dial does more for perceived price than any colour choice
raise_it_when: The product is premium, the reader is browsing, or the page has few items
lower_it_when: The page must hold many items, or it will be read at arm's length on a counter
breaks_at: Below 0.05 the type touches the trim edge and any print shop will cut into it

what_it_changes: Headline size relative to the canvas, so it holds at any output size
raise_it_when: The headline is the whole message and there is little else
lower_it_when: The headline is long, or the items below are the real content
breaks_at: Above 0.09 a four-word headline wraps to three lines and the hierarchy inverts

what_it_changes: Vertical distance from one list row to the next. Controls how many items fit and how calm the list reads
raise_it_when: The list is short and should feel unhurried
lower_it_when: More items must fit, or the reader is scanning to choose fast
breaks_at: Below 0.05 the descender of one row touches the cap of the next

what_it_changes: How much of the frame the picture takes before the copy starts
raise_it_when: The picture is the argument and the copy is a label
lower_it_when: There are proof lines, a price, and a button to fit
breaks_at: Above 0.58 the copy block runs into the button and the renderer refuses

what_it_changes: Space between lines inside one paragraph
raise_it_when: The text is long, the reader is reading rather than scanning, or the type is small
lower_it_when: The block must be compact, or the type is large and display-sized
breaks_at: Below 1.05 ascenders and descenders collide between lines

unit: number of accent colours in one artefact
what_it_changes: How many colours other than background and ink appear
raise_it_when: The design must direct attention to two competing actions
lower_it_when: One thing matters most, which is nearly always
breaks_at: At 4 nothing is emphasised, because emphasis is a ratio

unit: fraction of visible area carrying the accent
what_it_changes: How much of the surface the accent covers
raise_it_when: The artefact must be visible in a crowded feed at thumbnail size
lower_it_when: The positioning is premium, or the accent is a saturated red or orange
breaks_at: Above 0.25 the accent becomes the background and the real background becomes the accent

what_it_changes: How many typefaces are in use
raise_it_when: A display face genuinely does something the text face cannot
lower_it_when: Always, when in doubt — one family with real weight range beats two families
breaks_at: At 3 the artefact reads as a template someone filled in

what_it_changes: How many weights carry the hierarchy
raise_it_when: There are more than three levels of information to separate
lower_it_when: Hierarchy can be carried by size and space instead, which is quieter and ages better
breaks_at: At 5 the reader can no longer tell which level is which

unit: largest type size divided by body size
what_it_changes: The jump from body text to headline
raise_it_when: A single message must dominate; posters and covers live at the top of this range
lower_it_when: The page is dense with real content that all matters
breaks_at: Below 1.6 there is no hierarchy, only two sizes of the same thing

unit: fraction of an image frame kept empty for type
what_it_changes: How much of the picture is deliberately left with nothing in it
raise_it_when: Type will sit on the image, and long type needs more
lower_it_when: The type will sit beside or below the image instead
breaks_at: A reserve the scene fills is not a reserve; verify on the render, not in the prompt

unit: number of proof statements per artefact
what_it_changes: How many reasons-to-believe appear beside the claim
raise_it_when: The claim is large, the price is high, or the buyer is cold
lower_it_when: The reader already knows you, or the artefact is a reminder rather than an argument
breaks_at: Above 3 they stop being read as proof and start being read as text

what_it_changes: How many products, dishes or features one artefact carries
raise_it_when: The reader has decided to browse and wants the range
lower_it_when: The reader must choose in under a minute — a menu of 30 dishes sells fewer than a menu of 9
breaks_at: Above 14 at these pitches the renderer refuses and tells you the capacity

what_it_changes: The underlying division the layout snaps to
raise_it_when: Content sizes vary a lot and need many valid widths
lower_it_when: The artefact is simple and a coarse grid keeps it honest
breaks_at: At 1 nothing can sit beside anything, so every relationship becomes vertical

what_it_changes: How soft the boxes and buttons are
raise_it_when: The brand is friendly, digital, and app-adjacent
lower_it_when: The brand is editorial, industrial, or printed
breaks_at: Above 28 at this size buttons read as pills and the layout reads as a consumer app whatever else you do

what_it_changes: The thickness of dividing lines and bars
raise_it_when: A structure needs to be felt across the room, at a counter or on a poster
lower_it_when: The design is calm and the lines are only there to organise, not to speak
breaks_at: At 0 you have removed the structure rather than quietened it; use space instead

what_it_changes: How much surface noise and imperfection the imagery carries
raise_it_when: The frame must read as photographed rather than generated
lower_it_when: The output is going to print at high resolution, where grain compounds
breaks_at: At 0 across a whole set, every frame reads as generated even when nothing else is wrong
